notes: rnews.rs line 13: MAX_BATCH_DECOMPRESSED_BYTES = 50 MiB. MAX_RNEWS_ARTICLE_BYTES = 1 MiB. MAX_BATCH_ARTICLES = 1000. For a gunbatch (compressed) batch, after decompression the plain parser runs with the 50 MiB limit as the total decompressed size, but per-article capped at 1 MiB. So a gunbatch can only contain at most 50 articles at max article size (50 MiB / 1 MiB = 50), far below MAX_BATCH_ARTICLES = 1000. But for an uncompressed batch arriving via stdin, the stdin cap is 1 GiB, and up to 1000 articles at 1 MiB each = 1 GiB is possible. The two code paths have very different effective maximums with no documentation explaining why. This creates operator confusion (why can a gunbatch only carry ~50 max-size articles while a plain batch can carry 1000?). The constants should either be aligned and documented together, or the comment on MAX_BATCH_DECOMPRESSED_BYTES should note that it intentionally limits gunbatch capacity more aggressively than uncompressed batches as a gzip-bomb mitigation. This is a documentation/design clarity issue, not a correctness bug.
title: MAX_BATCH_DECOMPRESSED_BYTES (50 MiB) inconsistent with gunbatch article-count capacity
